text.p: Fidelity Investments is expanding its institutional retirement business in the U.S. by targetting small businesses and broadening the services offered to corporate clients, an official said Friday.
Robert Reynolds, head of the retirement group, said that sales of defined contribution plans to companies with under 1,000 employees had a record month in April.

"It's probably the high-growth area for number of plans because companies that have less than 1,000 employees -- 35 percent of them have 401K (plans)," Reynolds told Reuters in an interview in Washington.

Conversely, more than 90 percent of companies with more than 5,000 employees already have 401K retirement plans, although Fidelity has signed 13 new accounts in that area since the beginning of the year, he said.
Reynolds said the primary competitors in the market for retirement plans for smaller companies are insurance companies and regional banks.
Other fund companies which have tried to enter the market in recent years have been overwhelmed by the administrative burden of running retirement accounts, he said.
Last year, Fidelity joined the U.S. Chamber of Commerce to offer small businesses, mostly those with less than 100 employees, a low-cost streamlined retirement program.
Only about 25 percent of businesses with less than 100 workers have defined contribution programs.

Fidelity is also expanding the number of products available to corporate clients and will later this year offer a payroll administrative program in addition to other employee benefit services, Reynolds said.
Last week, Fidelity formed a separate unit within the institutional retirement group to offer benefits outsourcing, human resources, payroll adminstration and other employee services.
Thirty corporate accounts are already using its multi-benefit services, Reynolds said.

"The whole concept is providing an integrated platform to service employees where you can get it done cheaper, with a higher quality of service, so companies will be able to provide benefit programs with greater bang for their buck," he said.

Businesses of all size are demanding retirement accounts with mutual funds from more than one fund family, Reynolds said. To take advantage of that, Fidelity took a smaller version of its FundsNetwork mutual fund supermarket available to retail customers and applied it to the retirement business.
So far this year, Reynolds said the program, called FundsNet, has signed about $1 billion of new business.
"Plan sponsors are looking to diversify and we do see a demand for other fund families," he said. "Our goal was to have outside funds look like a Fidelity fund to a 401K plan participant," he added.
